A soldier attached to Operation Enduring Peace in Plateau State, Private Utim Terwase, has been rewarded with N500,000 for rejecting an identical amount allegedly offered as a bribe by a suspected notorious kidnapper. The spokesman for the military task force in Plateau State, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this in a statement issued in Jos on Wednesday. Oteh said Terwase apprehended the suspect following an attempted escape but refused to release him after the suspect allegedly offered him N500,000 in exchange for his freedom. He added that the soldier subsequently handed the suspect over to the appropriate authorities. In recognition of his integrity, discipline and commitment to duty, the Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Maj. Gen. Maxwell Dangana, rewarded Terwase with N500,000, matching the amount he reportedly rejected as a bribe. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Philimon Malgwi, as saying that the soldier’s conduct reflected the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty and commitment to duty expected of military personnel. 2027: Obi vows to pursue kidnappers into hideouts Soldiers rescue nine kidnap victims in Kebbi, recover 108 livestock Six abducted Benue mourners regain freedom He said, “Rather than compromise his responsibility for personal gain, he upheld the values of honesty, accountability and selfless service by discharging his duties responsibly.” According to the statement, Operation Enduring Peace considered Terwase’s action worthy of commendation and urged other personnel to emulate his exemplary conduct. It added that the recognition reinforced the operation’s commitment to promoting accountability, ethical conduct and professionalism in the discharge of its constitutional responsibilities. The military noted that the gesture sent a strong message to its personnel and Nigerians at large that honesty, accountability and professionalism remained important values worthy of recognition. It added that, at a time when corruption continued to undermine public trust, Terwase’s action served as a reminder that integrity was a personal choice, even when faced with temptation. “A soldier who refused N500,000 in dirty money has earned N500,000 in honour. Indeed, integrity pays!” the statement said. James Abraham
